summary: A scaffolded Next.js App Router starter that demonstrates Barkpark as a headless CMS backend — wiring schema definitions, a typed server-side fetch helper, and a seed script into a runnable site that developers get from `create-barkpark-app`.

intentions.title: Accelerate developer onboarding with a zero-to-running example
intentions.evidence: barkpark.config.ts.tmpl + package.json.tmpl scaffold a full Next.js project; seed.ts populates realistic authors/pages/posts so the first `pnpm dev` renders real content without manual data entry

intentions.title: Demonstrate the Barkpark query API surface (getDocs/getDoc/getDocBySlug)
intentions.evidence: lib/barkpark.ts exposes three typed helpers that cover the three read patterns (list, by id, by slug), serving as living documentation of /v1/data/query and /v1/data/doc endpoints

intentions.title: Teach Next.js App Router cache integration with Barkpark sync tags
intentions.evidence: lib/barkpark.ts sets next:{tags, revalidate:60} on every fetch, pairing cache tags in bp:ds:<dataset>:type:<type> / bp:ds:<dataset>:doc:<id> format that Barkpark's webhook revalidation can target

intentions.title: Show multi-workspace / scoped-prefix opt-in path
intentions.evidence: barkpark.config.ts.tmpl comments out BARKPARK_WORKSPACE/PROJECT; seed.ts builds a SCOPE string conditionally — both files teach the flat-vs-scoped routing split without forcing it on new users

intentions.title: Establish a canonical schema authoring pattern for content types
intentions.evidence: schemas/post.ts, schemas/author.ts, schemas/page.ts define richText, slug, reference, array fields as const objects matching the Barkpark schema contract, giving new projects a copy-paste starting point
